actions.justification: Immediate stroke team activation is required to coordinate rapid assessment and treatment for suspected stroke presentation.
Last known well time is critical to determine eligibility for thrombolysis (tPA within 4.5h) and mechanical thrombectomy (within 24h of LKW).
NIHSS score quantifies stroke severity, guides treatment decisions, and establishes baseline neurological status.
Mandatory initial assessment - hypoglycemia can mimic stroke and must be excluded immediately
Mandatory - identify atrial fibrillation or other cardiac arrhythmias as stroke etiology
Mandatory - required for IV tPA administration if eligible and for medication delivery
Mandatory lab workup (CBC, BMP, coagulation studies) required for stroke evaluation to assess for contraindications to thrombolytics and baseline hematologic/metabolic status.
Mandatory STAT CT head required to differentiate ischemic from hemorrhagic stroke before any treatment decisions, especially thrombolysis eligibility.
Assessing pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale is essential to establish baseline functional status, which impacts treatment decisions and outcome benchmarking for stroke patients.
Review CT head results to calculate ASPECTS score, which is critical for determining eligibility for thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke.
Early activation of neurointerventional team is essential in parallel with CT review to minimize door-to-intervention time if large vessel occlusion is identified.
Assess appropriateness of antiplatelet therapy pending CT results and determination of stroke type; contraindicated if hemorrhagic or if tPA is to be given.
Serial vital sign monitoring is essential for ongoing neurological assessment in a stroke patient, even with currently stable vitals. Continuous monitoring helps detect deterioration.
Hyperglycemia worsens stroke outcomes. Glucose monitoring and management is a standard stroke care measure per guidelines.
Hyperthermia increases metabolic demand in ischemic penumbra and worsens stroke outcomes. Temperature monitoring and management is recommended per stroke guidelines.

Blood pressure management targeting <180/105 is standard in acute stroke pending reperfusion therapy decision. Patient BP is currently 120/80 which is within acceptable range, but BP targets must be established and monitored actively during the acute stroke workup phase.
Patient with acute stroke presentation requires admission to stroke unit or ICU for continuous monitoring, serial neurological assessments, and coordinated stroke care per guidelines.
